item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports combining sequential and collaborative signals: [TGCL4SR (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) combines global temporal item-transition graphs with local sequence encoding; [GaGNN (2024)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002002552400536X) models individual and group transitions with separate encoders and information fusion. These motivate a complementary transition component, but do not establish that a simple sparse graph improves SASRec on this benchmark. For text, a [2026 hybrid study](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-431X/15/9/639) explicitly includes TF-IDF plus collaborative SVD using normalized-score late fusion. Its fixed fusion weights should not be assumed transferable to Amazon next-item ranking.\n\nPractical experiment inferred from these approaches: construct directed transition counts and item co-occurrence similarities from training histories only; prune each item’s neighbors for efficient sparse scoring. Fit local TF-IDF on available titles/descriptions, then compute candidate cosine similarity against a recency-weighted history profile. Fuse these signals with SASRec using normalized scores or reciprocal ranks, tuning a small weight grid separately for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. Evaluate graph-only, text-only, and combined additions; report every category alongside macro validation HR@10 under the pinned candidate protocol. This requires no pretrained weights or unavailable review attributes. Text similarity may capture related products while missing purchase direction; directed transitions offer a complementary signal. Treat any improvement as an empirical question, with zero-weight options allowing validation to reject an unhelpful component."}
